data.name: ProblemNone
data.value: (none)
data.comment: Shown in place of an expected or received value when there is none.

data.name: ProblemWrongAudienceDescription
data.value: The identity provider issued an ID token for another client, so JIM refused it.
data.comment: Sign-in problem description. 'ID token' is the OpenID Connect term.

data.name: ProblemWrongAudienceFix
data.value: Set {0} to the client ID the identity provider registered for JIM's portal.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a JIM setting (an environment variable); never translate it.

data.name: ProblemWrongIssuerDescription
data.value: The ID token came from an issuer JIM does not accept.

data.name: ProblemApiWrongAudienceDescription
data.value: An access token the identity provider issued was refused because it is not for JIM's API.

data.name: ProblemApiWrongAudienceFix
data.value: JIM expects the audience {0} names when it is an api:// URI, and otherwise the portal's client ID, {1}. Change that setting, or have the identity provider issue the audience JIM expects.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the names of JIM settings; never translate them.

data.name: ProblemApiWrongIssuerDescription
data.value: An access token came from an issuer JIM does not accept.

data.name: ProblemMissingClaimDescription
data.value: JIM could not tell who signed in, because the sign-in carried no '{0}' claim.
data.comment: {0} is a claim type, for example 'sub'.

data.name: ProblemMissingClaimFix
data.value: Set {0} to a claim the identity provider issues for everyone, or have it issue '{1}'.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a JIM setting; {1} is a claim type.

data.name: ProblemEntraVersion1Fix
data.value: Microsoft Entra ID issued a version 1 access token. Set requestedAccessTokenVersion to 2 in the app registration's manifest (Register-JIMIdentityProvider -Provider EntraId does), so its tokens carry the client ID as their audience and come from the tenant's version 2 issuer, which is what JIM accepts.
data.comment: requestedAccessTokenVersion and the cmdlet are code; never translate them.

data.name: ProblemIssuerFix
data.value: If that issuer is your identity provider's, add it to {0} along with those listed; otherwise check that {1} names the identity provider people sign in with.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the names of JIM settings.

data.name: ProblemInvalidClientDescription
data.value: The identity provider did not accept JIM's portal client.

data.name: ProblemInvalidClientExpected
data.value: the identity provider to accept client '{0}' and its secret
data.comment: Completes 'Expected:'. {0} is a client ID.

data.name: ProblemInvalidClientFix
data.value: Check that {0} names the portal's client, and that {1} holds its current secret. Register-JIMIdentityProvider -ResetClientSecret makes a new one.
data.comment: {0} and {1} are the names of JIM settings.

data.name: ProblemUnauthorizedClientDescription
data.value: The identity provider does not let JIM's portal client sign people in this way.

data.name: ProblemUnauthorizedClientExpected
data.value: client '{0}' to sign people in with an authorisation code
data.comment: Completes 'Expected:'. {0} is a client ID.

data.name: ProblemUnauthorizedClientFix
data.value: Check that {0} names the portal's client, and that the identity provider lets it use the authorisation code flow.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a JIM setting.

data.name: ProblemInvalidScopeDescription
data.value: The identity provider refused the scopes JIM asked for.

data.name: ProblemInvalidScopeFix
data.value: Set {0} to a scope the identity provider grants JIM's portal client, or leave it empty.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a JIM setting.

data.name: LockoutWarning
data.value: Sign-in depends on '{0}'. This change stops everyone signing in to JIM, including you. Until another certificate is trusted for sign-in, only the infrastructure API key can put it right.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a certificate.

data.name: LockoutWarningForHost
data.value: Sign-in depends on '{0}': it is the only certificate JIM trusts for {1}. This change stops everyone signing in to JIM, including you. Until another certificate is trusted for sign-in, only the infrastructure API key can put it right.
data.comment: {0} is the name of a certificate, {1} the identity provider's host name.
